13	# Agent Deployment Rules
14	
15	**Enforcement Level**: HIGH
16	These rules apply when working with agent definitions and multi-provider deployment.
17	
18	## Agent Ecosystem
19	
20	### Categories
21	
22	**General-Purpose Writing Agents** (`agentic/code/agents/`):
23	- `writing-validator` - Validates voice consistency and authenticity
24	- `prompt-optimizer` - Enhances prompts using AIWG principles
25	- `content-diversifier` - Generates varied examples and perspectives
26	
27	**SDLC Framework Agents** (`agentic/code/frameworks/sdlc-complete/agents/`):
28	- 64 specialized agents covering all SDLC phases
29	- See `@$AIWG_ROOT/agentic/code/frameworks/sdlc-complete/agents/manifest.json` for complete list
30	
31	**Marketing Agents** (`agentic/code/frameworks/media-marketing-kit/agents/`):
32	- 37 marketing-focused agents covering campaign lifecycle
33	- See `@$AIWG_ROOT/agentic/code/frameworks/media-marketing-kit/agents/manifest.json` for complete list
34	
35	## Multi-Provider Support
36	
37	### Deployment Commands
38	
39	```bash
40	# Claude Code (default - creates .claude/agents/)
41	aiwg -deploy-agents --mode sdlc
42	
43	# GitHub Copilot (creates .github/agents/*.yaml + copilot-instructions.md)
44	aiwg -deploy-agents --provider copilot --mode sdlc
45	
46	# Factory AI (creates .factory/droids/ + AGENTS.md)
47	aiwg -deploy-agents --provider factory --mode sdlc --deploy-commands --create-agents-md
48	
49	# OpenCode (creates .opencode/agent/ + AGENTS.md)
50	aiwg -deploy-agents --provider opencode --mode sdlc --deploy-commands --create-agents-md
51	
52	# Cursor (creates .cursor/rules/ + AGENTS.md)
53	aiwg -deploy-agents --provider cursor --mode sdlc --deploy-commands --create-agents-md
54	
55	# OpenAI/Codex (creates .codex/agents/)
56	aiwg -deploy-agents --provider openai
57	
58	# As single AGENTS.md file
59	aiwg -deploy-agents --provider openai --as-agents-md
60	```
61	
62	### Model Override
63	
64	Default models defined in `agentic/code/frameworks/sdlc-complete/config/models.json`.
65	
66	```bash
67	aiwg -deploy-agents --provider factory \
68	  --reasoning-model <your-reasoning-model> \
69	  --coding-model <your-coding-model> \
70	  --efficiency-model <your-efficiency-model>
71	```
72	
73	### Provider-Specific Guidance
74	
75	- **Factory AI**: See `agentic/code/frameworks/sdlc-complete/agents/factory-compat.md`
76	- **OpenCode**: See `docs/integrations/opencode-quickstart.md`
77	- **Cursor**: See `docs/integrations/cursor-quickstart.md`
78	- **OpenAI/Codex**: See `agentic/code/frameworks/sdlc-complete/agents/openai-compat.md`
79	
80	## Agent Definition Format
81	
82	### Metadata Structure
83	
84	```yaml
85	---
86	name: agent-name
87	description: Brief agent description
88	model: claude-sonnet-5|claude-opus-5|claude-haiku-4-5  # Pin variant. Bare aliases inherit parent-context attributes — under a 1M-context parent (`claude-opus-5[1m]`), subagent dispatch hits the usage-credit gate. See aiwg #1442.
89	tools: Read, Write, MultiEdit, Bash, WebFetch, Glob, Grep
90	orchestration: true|false
91	category: sdlc-setup|sdlc-orchestration|sdlc-management|...
92	---
93	
94	# Agent Name
95	
96	[Agent instructions and capabilities]
97	```
98	
99	### Model Variant Pinning (CRITICAL)
100	
101	Always pin a specific model variant in agent/skill/command frontmatter. Bare aliases (`sonnet`, `opus`, `haiku`) are resolved by the parent platform session. When the parent runs on a 1M-context variant such as `opus[1m]`, the alias resolution inherits 1M-context attributes and any subagent dispatch hits the credit-gated path:
102	
103	```
104	API Error: Usage credits required for 1M context · run /usage-credits to turn them on, or /model to switch to standard context
105	```
106	
107	Use the pinned 500K-context variants for AIWG agents:
108	
109	| Bare alias (forbidden) | Pinned variant (required) | Notes |
110	|---|---|---|
111	| `model: sonnet` | `model: claude-sonnet-5` | Default balanced workhorse |
112	| `model: opus` | `model: claude-opus-5` | Complex reasoning (non-1M) |
113	| `model: haiku` | `model: claude-haiku-4-5` | Fast/simple tasks |
114	
115	`aiwg doctor` flags any agent/skill/command frontmatter using a bare alias.
116	
117	### Tool Selection Guidelines
118	
119	| Task Type | Recommended Tools |
120	|-----------|------------------|
121	| Code analysis | Read, Glob, Grep |
122	| Code modification | Read, Write, MultiEdit |
123	| Build/test execution | Bash |
124	| Research | WebFetch, WebSearch |
125	| File discovery | Glob, Grep |
126	
127	## Working with Agents
128	
129	### Parallel Execution Pattern
130	
131	Launch multiple agents in a single message:
132	
133	```
134	Task(security-architect) -> Security validation
135	Task(test-architect) -> Testability review
136	Task(requirements-analyst) -> Requirements traceability
137	Task(technical-writer) -> Clarity and consistency
138	```
139	
140	### Agent Isolation
141	
142	All agents work independently with isolated contexts regardless of platform. Each agent:
143	- Has its own context window
144	- Cannot directly communicate with other agents
145	- Returns results to the orchestrator for synthesis
146
